questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As someone studying biology, the beautiful, unique and different nature was very interesting and important for me. It was also important that I could choose meaningful courses within subjects that interest me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The university was very helpful and communicated clearly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None. However, if I had lived in a student accommodation, I would have been picked in the airport and been brought to my accommodation free of charge.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was a bit confused about what the orientation week was going to consist of, as there was only one official international orientation day arranged by the university. The main activities besides that were organized by an international student organization and was super fun and brought a lot of new connections. However, I did not know about most of the activities until shortly before they happened.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I had a really great off-campus flat experience. My flatmates were all kiwis and they were just wonderful. However, I was very isolated from the other exchange students. Almost everyone live on campus and it is 100x easier to join social activities on campus. Living on campus is more expensive, but it is expensive to take the bus to campus as well, so in the end, the price is probably the same. I personally was very lucky with my flatmates and I really enjoyed having a more authentic experience, as this is how most kiwis in Auckland live. I also still made friends with international students and did some trips with them etc., and I could definitely have joined more things if I wanted (but most of my social life was with my flatmates). Would personally not change a thing, I loved it! But it's two very different experiences living on-campus and off-campus, I think. If you want that classic "exchange student bubble" experience, 100% live on campus!!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You are guaranteed campus accommodation as an international student, if you apply on time.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They had a platform that you need to register through. Got an e-mail with instructions. You can drop/change courses until two weeks (I think) into the semester, which is nice because it gives you the chance of trying out the class. Was working fine, but took a while to get familiar with the platform and understand how the process works.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: E-mailing the international office. When being here physically, you can drop by their Student Hubs for help (long lines in beginning of semester though!).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wanted to pick a few master courses (I'm a bachelor student), and they were quite strict about that. Couldn't just sign up for them. It was a long process. I had to e-mail the course coordinator and explain my situation and convince them that I had the academic skills to take the course. In the end, it worked out with one of the master courses, so that was nice (however I actually ended up dropping that one but oh well).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the type of assessments the courses have. It matters quite a lot for how stressful the semester feels and it's very different from course to course. Some don't have exams (yay!) and only do assessments through quizzes, reports etc. Some have more big assignments than others. So definitely something to consider!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Appropiate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Different with all the different types of assessments throughout the semester. I wasn't used to that, so that was a bit stressful to navigate, especially in the beginning.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIOSCI 394
BIOSCI 334
MARINE 303

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
BIOSCI 394 is super nice. It had two cool field trips, the lecturers were really sweet aaaaand it did not have a final exam!! 
BIOSCI 334 is also a very interesting course for people interested in marine biology. Very interesting topics! I learned a lot and enjoyed the lectures. However, the practical part of the course was a bit boring, no field work and mainly just Excel-stuff.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Was only allowed to bring 3 months of medicine so had to pay to go to the doctor and for the medicine, as this was not covered by my travel insurance. Was quite expensive (around 1000 DKK in total). However, I think it might have been covered by the student insurance that you could get through the university, but I didn't have that one.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Loads of cool clubs to sign up for! Really cool club-culture. Also an international student organization.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The tramping club was super duper cool (AUTC). Also the international student organisation (SASS).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore nature and wildlife!!! Take a trip to the South Island during your stay, very beautiful nature. In the North Island, explore Tongariro (Mount Doom hehe), Bay of Islands and the beautiful beaches. Tawharanui Regional Park and Tiritiri Mathangi Island if interested in birds!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are super kind and friendly, more open than in Denmark!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Consider what type of experience you want when deciding where to live. Do you want are more authentic, local experience? Consider living in a shared flat with people that seem nice! Do you want a more "socially safe", international experience? Live on campus.
2. Consider what is important for you regarding your courses and read about the course assessments. I know exchange students that had way more free time than me and no exams because they prioritized that. I could have done that too, but that would have meant that I had to choose some courses I was not as passionate about. So it's something to think about.
3. Get out of the city and enjoy the beautiful nature! To do that: make friends with someone who has a car or buy a car :) I did the latter and it gave me so much freedom. Bought an old one and sold it again in the end of my exchange. It made sense because I also did not live in the city center

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends on the other side of the globe. Going on exciting adventures in beautiful nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Comparing myself with other exchange students and having unrealistically high expectations for all the things I should be doing as an exchange student. After all, although you are at an amazing location and are having a great adventure, you are also still a student with obligations. You need to make space for assignments, but also for chill days once in a while. And then at the same time, time flies so fast! The balance was hard and I felt stressed at times.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
